Redhawks cruise past Lockport 42-21 in senior night victory

Lola Schwerha, Content Managing Editor
September 6, 2026
Gallery • 4 Photos
Tianyao He
Senior running back Landon Nelson pummels towards the endzone and secures a touchdown for the Redhawks. Nelson would go on to play a big role in the Redhawks' big win.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:26
Instaread

Senior night could not have scripted a more dramatic opening act for the Redhawks. Taking the opening kickoff, junior Mark Williams set the tone immediately with an electrifying 33-yard return straight into Lockport territory.

ReserveBaseball Tickets

The Redhawks capitalized fast. A Lockport face-mask penalty set up first-and-goal with 7:22 left in the first quarter, paving the way for senior Landon Nelson to punch in the game’s first touchdown at the 6:45 mark for a quick 7-0 lead.

Discover more

Sports
Book Walking Tours

The second quarter built on that momentum. Sophomore Ian Figi doubled the lead to 14-0 with 11:50 remaining, followed immediately by a massive defensive stop on fourth-and-1 to force a turnover on downs.

Moments later, senior Kyle Clark engineered a key highlight on offense. He tipped a wild, bouncing deflection straight to junior Owen Render to secure an improbable first down at 8:33 left. Junior Ryan Jacobson finished the drive with a touchdown with 7:36 remaining to stretch the lead to 21-0.

When Lockport broke loose on a potential house call, junior Eron Kennedy refused to give up, sprinting downfield to make a game-saving tackle at the 7:26 mark.

Lockport finally got on the board with 5:24 left in the quarter to make it 21-7, but Clark answered instantly with a soaring 37-yard kickoff return. Nelson took over from there, capping the drive with a touchdown at the 2:31 mark to push the score to 28-7.

For Nelson, every yard carried extra personal weight after recovering from an injury he suffered against the same opponent last year.

“Last season, I had a season-ending injury against Lockport,” Nelson said. “My whole year was just being determined to beat this team fully, and I wanted to be really physical against them. I’m really glad we did that.”

GetExecutive Coaching

Though a dynamic Nathaniel Yoon interception was wiped away by a pass interference penalty, junior Hari Santhanam pounced on a clutch fumble recovery with 1:10 left to send the home crowd into a frenzy heading into the half.

The dominant opening half came after a demanding week of preparation and team-building behind the scenes.

“We spent time this week working together, talking together,” head coach Mike Ulriech said. “Part of it is just, the hardest thing is to build a team out of a bunch of individuals. We just needed to work on this aspect this weekend, being on the same page, communicating together. Offensively, we had an ugly week at practice, and some hard conversations, but they paid off. We played really well tonight.”

The Redhawks kept their foot on the gas in the third quarter. With 7:55 left in the quarter, Williams tore through the defense to elevate the lead to 35-7.

Lockport answered with a touchdown with 2:09 left, but a 24-yard burst by Nelson late in the third quarter quickly reclaimed control of the game’s tempo.

Early in the final quarter, Williams delivered the crown jewel, breaking loose for a jaw-dropping 40-yard touchdown sprint.

Lockport tacked on a late score with two minutes remaining, but the outcome was already sealed. Powered by relentless special teams, clutch defensive takeaways, and a balanced offensive attack, the Redhawks locked up a commanding 42-21 victory to give their senior class a memorable home farewell.

GetExecutive Coaching

“Hopefully more than anything tonight guys realize that they can trust themselves, that they can trust their team, and they can trust their coaches, and good things are going to happen,” Ulreich said.”
